# Kawahara capillary–gravity waves {#sec-kawahara}

`apps/kawahara` — the only *dispersive* model in the report: fifth order, and
its linear symbol is purely imaginary.

## Physical setting

Long weakly nonlinear waves on a shallow fluid layer where surface tension and
gravity both matter. Where the Korteweg–de Vries equation keeps only
third-order dispersion, Kawahara (1972) retains the fifth-order term as well.
When the two have opposite signs they compete, and the resulting dispersion
relation is non-monotonic — waves of different length can travel in opposite
directions.

## Governing equations

$$
\partial_t u \;+\; \alpha\,u\,\partial_x u
  \;-\; \beta\,\partial_x^3 u
  \;+\; \gamma\,\partial_x^5 u \;=\; 0 .
$$ {#eq-kw-pde}

::: {.callout-note}
## Sign convention

This application defines $\beta$ with a minus sign in @eq-kw-pde. To use a
coefficient $b$ multiplying $+u_{xxx}$, set $\beta = -b$.
:::

## Spectral formulation

Odd derivatives transform to odd powers of $ik$, so the symbol is **purely
imaginary**:

$$
L(k) \;=\; -i\,\omega(k), \qquad \omega(k) \;=\; \beta k^3 + \gamma k^5 .
$$ {#eq-kw-symbol}

The quadratic flux $\alpha u\,\partial_x u = \tfrac{\alpha}{2}\partial_x(u^2)$
is evaluated as $N = u^2$ with

$$
M_{\mathrm{nl}}(k) \;=\; -i\,\frac{\alpha}{2}\,k_x .
$$ {#eq-kw-nl}

This is the qualitative difference from every other spectral chapter here.
An even-order dissipative operator has $L$ real and negative: $|e^{L\Delta t}|<1$
and modes **decay**. Here $L$ is imaginary, so $|e^{L\Delta t}| = 1$ exactly and
modes **rotate** — the amplitude of each Fourier component is preserved and only
its phase advances. ETD is not damping anything; it is applying an exact phase
rotation.

The phase velocity follows from @eq-kw-symbol:

$$
c_p(k) \;=\; \frac{\omega(k)}{k} \;=\; \beta k^2 + \gamma k^4 ,
$$ {#eq-kw-phase}

which changes sign at $k^2 = -\beta/\gamma$ when $\beta\gamma < 0$. Below that
wave number waves travel one way, above it the other. The defaults
$\alpha = 1$, $\beta = 1$, $\gamma = -1$ put the model in this competing
regime.

## Solution strategy

ETD1 as in @eq-etd1, dealiased — the quadratic nonlinearity doubles the
highest wave number present, so the 2/3 rule is required.

## Verification

* **Phase velocity.** A single mode advances at $c_p(k)$ from
  @eq-kw-phase, checked independently for the $k^3$ and $k^5$ branches.
* **Manufactured solutions.** Independent manufactured-solution tests for
  third- and fifth-order dispersion.
* **Mean preservation.** The $\mathbf{k}=0$ mode is untouched.

## Binaries and inputs

`kawahara` (CPU), `kawahara_hip`. Preset `pulse.json` (256-point line).

## Scalability

Not measured.
